children: A private gauge showed China's service-sector activity expanded at a faster pace in August, rebounding from a sharp slowdown in July, amid faster growth in new business and stronger hiring in the sector.
The RatingDog Services purchasing managers' index compiled by S&P Global rose to 51.4 in August from 50.4 in July, according to data released Thursday.
The private gauge pointed to a better result than the official measure, which showed service activity remained unchanged from a month earlier.

The new business subindex rose at a faster pace, recovering from July's four-month low, on stronger domestic demand, RatingDog said. New export orders expanded for a fourth consecutive month in August, but at a slower pace, continuing to ease from June's 20-month high.

The subindex tracking employment in the service sector expanded for a fourth consecutive month, the longest streak of job creation since 2023, with the pace of growth accelerating to one of the strongest levels in the past three years, RatingDog said.
"Business sentiment regarding the 12-month outlook improved from July's recent low," said Yao Yu, founder of RatingDog.

Average input prices rose for the 18th consecutive month in August due to rising costs from labor, materials and fuel prices. Output prices increased for a third consecutive month, the longest streak of price rises since the first half of 2024, with the pace of increase unchanged from July and remaining marginal, said RatingDog.
